body.target_estimand: The observed-law target is \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) for \(a\in J\). Under the frozen model this functional is not identified with \(\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y(a)]\) uniformly over full-data witnesses; an additional condition linking realized-dose consistency to deterministic-dose sections is required for that causal equality.

sampling_model.design: The observed sample is iid from \(P\in\mathcal M\). Although membership requires at least one full-data extension satisfying consistency, sectionwise conditional exchangeability, and conditional-potential-mean continuity, those conditions do not force all admissible extensions to agree on \(\mathbb E[Y(a)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The frozen description names boundary-corrected local-polynomial learners with bandwidth \(n^{-1/(2s)}\), but it does not yet specify a complete sample map. The advertised exponents are derived conditionally on a regular kernel, uniformly invertible boundary moment system, normalization map, and singular-matrix convention; the centered validation-fold V-statistic bound remains open.
sampling_model.overlap: The conditional density \(g(a\mid w)\) is bounded above and away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous dose \(A_i\in[0,1]\), with inference restricted to \(J=[\delta,1-\delta]\).
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(W_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with compact covariates and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The limiting distribution is the integral of the difference of the squared constrained and unconstrained slope processes.
We study the extremal behavior of the stationary argmax process on increasing intervals.
A suitably standardized supremum of the Grenander-type estimation error converges to a standard Gumbel random variable.
The confidence intervals concern the continuous treatment effect curve at a fixed point and invert a likelihood-ratio-type test.
The paper provides general conditions for consistency and pointwise convergence of generalized Grenander-type estimators.
Approximation results for the supremum of an empirical process yield asymptotically valid uniform confidence bands.
The paper develops a bootstrap procedure for constructing uniform confidence bands from weighted local-linear estimation.

body.tldr: The frozen assumptions do not identify an exact-dose causal curve, and the Brownian--GCM likelihood-ratio excursion law needed for simultaneous calibration remains open. What is proved is narrower but exact: fixed-location finite-dimensional stationarity; Brownian dilation and the deterministic action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\) with an explicit plateau witness; conditional nuisance and transfer algebra; the spatial-volume clock; conditional centering calculus; and deterministic profile inversion. The construction is therefore an observed-law LR profiling architecture, not a calibrated simultaneous causal band or a validated Gumbel procedure.

project_justification.gap: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) provide the fixed-location Brownian--GCM LR functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) analyze a distinct Markov argmax process, and Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) analyze slope-error extremes. None supplies the infinite-domain contact-set LDP, sharp Palm expansion, anticlustering, marked-Poisson law, or grid theorem for the LR-energy field. Separately, the frozen causal assumptions admit observed-equivalent full-data extensions with different exact-dose causal means.
project_justification.niche: The actionable research niche is now an open-problem program: repair exact-dose causal identification, then establish the LR-energy contact-set excursion mechanism and a uniform optimized-statistic transfer. The deterministic action and clock calculations identify the correct objects without claiming the missing probability law.
project_justification.fill: This round proves the exact Brownian/GCM dilation, the action bracket \(1/2\le I_\star\le9/8\), a compact plateau witness, finite-dimensional stationarity, conditional learner-rate exponents, product and plug-in remainder algebra, a fixed-kernel validation-fold calculation, deterministic optimized-value stability under explicit localization/envelope premises, the exact spatial clock, conditional centering substitution, profile interval structure, crossing containment, and homogeneous reduction. It leaves the excursion, continuum transfer, simulation, and coverage steps open.

body.related_work: Banerjee and Wellner (2001) are used only for the finite fixed-location Brownian--GCM LR functional. Hooghiemstra and Lopuhaä (1998) obtain extremes for a different Markov argmax process with explicit transition machinery; Durot, Kulikov, and Lopuhaä (2012) transfer slope-error extremes, not LR-energy excursions. Doss (2026) supplies neighboring fixed-dose causal-isotonic LR work, while Takatsu and Westling (2025), Ai, Huang, and Zhang (2026), and Doss--VandenBerg develop neighboring simultaneous-band approaches. The present proved results neither tighten those probability theorems nor establish optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact identity \(\Pr\{D(0)>u\}=\Pr\{\Phi(u^{-1/2}\mathbb W)>1\}\) identifies the candidate small-noise scaling, and the action lies between \(1/2\) and \(9/8\). No infinite-domain LDP connects that action to a logarithmic tail, and even a logarithmic equivalent would not supply the additive ratio or Palm prefactor. Missing pieces are contact-set exponential tightness and continuity, minimizer classification modulo translation, fluctuation and multiplicity analysis, conditional cluster-shape control, anticlustering, marked-Poisson approximation, and a sample-path grid theorem. Statistically, the learner is not a single specified map and optimized LR transfer still lacks a fitted-kernel maximal inequality, common localization, and a slope envelope.
body.honest_scope: No exact-dose causal identification theorem, sharp LR excursion theorem, growing-domain coupling, feasible Gumbel calibration, simulated-grid approximation, or nominal simultaneous coverage theorem is proved. The profile threshold is left arbitrary, and inversion preserves only the probability of its common LR event. The central cluster mechanism remains an explicit open question. No claim is made about optimal width, tuning freedom, or dominance over Doss--VandenBerg multiscale Gaussian bands.
body.interpretation: The estimand \(\theta(a)=\int m(a,w)p(w)\,dw\) is an observed-law G-computation curve on \(J\). Under the frozen assumptions it is not uniformly equal to the exact-dose causal mean. For the AHA/CMS nurse-hours--readmission application, the current mathematics supports an observed-law isotonic LR profile and a deterministic way to map any common profile event into threshold-crossing sets; it does not support reporting those sets as calibrated simultaneous causal confidence sets.
